subject: Private deploy: gateway safety checklist + routing clarifications
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice@avalonhealth.com>, Samir Patel <samir.p@avalonhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private deploy: gateway safety checklist + routing clarifications

Hi Alice / Samir —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Before we spin up the private deployment in your VPC we have a very small set of safety/regulatory checks the infra team needs to confirm so the activation window goes smoothly. I pulled the items below from our standard preflight and flagged the few questions where we need your input.

Short checklist (please confirm Y/N or provide values where requested):
- Public egress gateway: will outbound traffic be NATed behind a single egress IP, or multiple elastic IPs? (provide IPs if applicable)
- Inbound routing: do you require a static NAT from our bastion to your VPN appliance? If so, which static IP should we present?
- Port allowlist: we recommend opening 443, 10250 (kube), 50051 (gRPC) and 27017-27019 only between our pods and the customer-managed DB subnet. Confirm any additional DB ports.
- TLS inspection / MITM devices: are there enterprise TLS proxies that will terminate and re-encrypt traffic? If yes, provide CA cert upload method.
- KMS connectivity: will your KMS be reachable from the Redwood private control plane subnets? If not, we need an offline key-exchange plan.
- Logging & retention: confirm S3 bucket target for audit logs and required retention (days).

Questions we flagged for Avalon:
1) Gateway ciphers: we ship a default cipher set; do you have any disallowed ciphers or FIPS requirements?
2) Service account egress: for telemetry, our runtime calls home to telemetry.redwood.com — can we allow outbound on 443 to telemetry.redwood.com, or does that need to go through a proxy?
3) Failover routing: if your primary peering path degrades, do we fail to an alternate peering or pause traffic? (we can support either via routing policy)

Attachments: gateway-ports-and-ciphers.csv (port/cipher recommended baseline), redwood-preflight-checklist.pdf (full preflight).

If you can answer items in-line below I'm happy to mark this ready; if it's easier, let's take 20 minutes to walk the network team through on Wednesday. Proposed time: Wed 2027-01-20 10:00 PT.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Alice Monroe <alice@avalonhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.p@avalonhealth.com>, Avalon Health - Network Team <network@avalonhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 11:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Private deploy: gateway safety checklist + routing clarifications

Ben —

Thanks for the clear list. Answers inline: 

- Public egress gateway: We will NAT outbound through our egress cluster which currently uses two Elastic IPs. I'll attach the IPs in a follow-up note from our network team; Samir is looping them in.
- Inbound routing: We prefer presenting a static IP from your side for VPN handoff. Can you confirm the IP you'll present?
- Port allowlist: 443 and 10250 OK. For the DB we need 27017-27019 open to our database subnet 10.12.32.0/24.
- TLS inspection: We do have a TLS proxy that re‑signs with an internal CA for outbound traffic (only on egress to internet). We will provide the CA bundle via the secure drive link.
- KMS: KMS is reachable only from our management VPCs; we'll create an interface endpoint for the Redwood control plane.
- Logging & retention: S3 target: s3://avalon-redwood-logs, retention 365 days.

Answers to flagged items:
1) FIPS: Yes, production clusters are FIPS-enabled; please ensure modules are FIPS-compliant.
2) Telemetry: outbound to telemetry.redwood.com must go via our HTTP proxy at proxy-internal.avalon:8080. We will provide proxy creds via secure artifact.
3) Failover: prefer failover to the alternate peering; do not pause traffic.

I'll have network upload gateway IPs and CA bundle by EOD. Can confirm Wed 10:00 PT works for the call.

--
Alice Monroe
VP, IT Operations
Avalon Health

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 12:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deploy: gateway safety checklist + routing clarifications

Ben / Kim —

Quick technical notes after reading Avalon's replies:
- Static IP for inbound: we can present a single EIP from our bastion pool. I'll confirm the exact IPs after the call (need to reserve them in the activation window).
- FIPS: we need to switch to the FIPS cipher profile. That will change our default TLS module — Kim, can you confirm which of our runtime components require an explicit FIPS flag at deploy time?
- Proxy for telemetry: if traffic must traverse their internal proxy, we'll need to configure HTTP_PROXY + credentials at runtime and adjust our health checks to proxy through. Also need to ensure OCSP stapling still functions through the proxy.
- KMS reachability: good that they'll create an interface endpoint. We'll still require a route table entry from the control plane subnets to the endpoint; include that in the network runbook.

I'll be on the Wed call to confirm IP reservations and to walk through the port/cipher CSV.

-Marcus
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Great — thanks for the speedy replies and the confirmations, Alice. Next steps confirmed so we have clear owners and timeline before activation: 

1) Avalon to upload: EIP list + CA bundle + proxy credential artifact (Alice / Samir) — target: EOD Tue 2027-01-19 (noted you'll aim for EOD; if delayed please ping).
2) Redwood to reserve: single EIP for inbound VPN, confirm EIP value on the Wed 10:00 PT call (Marcus).
3) Redwood infra: set FIPS flag across runtime components and prepare FIPS artifact notes for the compliance runbook (Kimberly).
4) Network run-through call: Wed 2027-01-20 10:00 PT — dial-in link: https://meet.redwood.com/avalon-preflight (Marcus / Ben / Alice / Samir + network ops).

We'll hold the activation window until we've verified the interface endpoint and S3 logging access. After today's call we'll capture the exact gating checklist to JIRA INF-5923 and attach the artifacts.

If anything changes before Wed, please reply to this thread. Looking forward to the call.

Best —
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: gateway-ports-and-ciphers.csv, redwood-preflight-checklist.pdf
